title: Therapeutic potential of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles as a cell-free approach in autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis of preclinical studies.
authors: Mohtashami T, Aghayan AH, Masoudi A, Atashi A, Garmabi B, Jamalpoor Z, Khaksari M
abstract: BACKGROUND: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is an intricate neurodevelopmental condition distinguished by challenges in social interaction, repetitive behavioral patterns, and neuroinflammation, with limited effective treatments. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) offer a promising cell-free therapy due to their immunomodulatory and regenerative properties. This study evaluates their therapeutic efficacy in preclinical ASD models. METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis, searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science. The SYRCLE tool assessed risk of bias. Standardized mean difference (SMD) was calculated using a random-effects model to evaluate MSC-EV effects on sociability, repetitive behaviors, and inflammatory cytokines. Subgroup analysis, sensitivity analysis, and publication bias assessment addressed heterogeneity. RESULTS: Five studies (2018-2024) were included. MSC-EV-treated mice showed significant improvements in sociability (SMD =1.34, 95% CI:0.68-2.76), reduced repetitive behaviors (SMD =-1.12, 95% CI:-0.65 to -1.59), and modulated neuroinflammation, with decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, SMD = -2.28, 95% CI:-0.33 to -4.24 and TNF-a, SMD = -1.22, 95% CI:-0.47 to -1.97 and IL-6, SMD = -1.03, 95% CI:-0.38 to -1.68) and increased IL-10 (SMD =0.58, 95% CI:0.03-1.13). Subgroup analysis indicated umbilical cord- and adipose-derived MSC-EVs had superior efficacy. CONCLUSION: MSC-EVs demonstrate significant therapeutic potential in preclinical ASD models by improving core symptoms and modulating inflammation. However, limited studies and heterogeneity highlight the need for standardized protocols and further preclinical research to facilitate clinical translation.

title: Advances and perspectives in genetically encoded biosensors for biomarker detection and theranostic circuits.
authors: Xu J, Qi Q, Wang Q
abstract: Effective biomarker detection is critical for timely and accurate clinical disease diagnosis. However, conventional analytical methodologies are often constrained by laborious procedures, reliance on specialized equipment, and an inherent inability to perform continuous in situ monitoring. To circumvent these limitations, synthetic biology has pioneered the development of genetically encoded biosensors as a rapid, highly sensitive, and cost-effective alternative. This review specifically focuses on transcriptional regulation-based biosensors, primarily those utilizing allosteric transcription factors (aTFs) and two-component systems (TCSs). By integrating these regulatory sensing modules into engineered microbial chassis, researchers can achieve continuous, real-time biomarker monitoring even within complex and otherwise inaccessible physiological environments. This review particularly focuses on microbial chassis rather than mammalian systems due to their highly tractable genetics, rapid response kinetics, and their unique potential to be deployed as autonomous living probiotics for in situ theranostics. Furthermore, coupling these sensors with engineered actuator genes enables the construction of intelligent therapeutic genetic circuits. This closed-loop theranostic paradigm facilitates simultaneous, real-time diagnosis and autonomous, localized therapeutic interventions, paving the way for personalized and dose-adaptive precision medicine. Finally, we summarize recent advancements in these biosensor platforms, explore their applications in targeted disease interventions, and discuss the contemporary challenges alongside future perspectives for their clinical translation.

title: A CRISPR/Cas14a-based platform for sensitive and specific single-nucleotide variant detection via short single-strand DNA amplification and split target design.
authors: Hu Y, Liao Y, Wang X, Yuan T, Qiao L, Luo Y, Pan S, Li X
abstract: Single-nucleotide variant (SNV) detection, including tumor-associated mutation detection and pharmacogenetic genotyping, holds significant clinical value. Among current methods, CRISPR/Cas14a-based approaches offer advantages in specificity, sensitivity, and efficiency. However, the inherent single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) targeting property of Cas14a limits its direct application to genomic DNA detection, and its specificity requires further optimization to meet clinical standards. Here, we developed a CRISPR/Cas14a system based on short ssDNA amplification and split target design (SAST), which substantially enhances specificity through split target design while achieving high sensitivity via short ssDNA amplification. Experimental results demonstrate that SAST system achieves a Concentration LOD (limit of detection) of 100 aM for target DNA and a MAF (mutant allele frequency) LOD of 0.00001% in simulated samples. The platform was successfully validated for SNV detection in tumor samples (KRAS G12D, rs121913529, c.35G > A) and pharmacogenetic genotyping (CYP2C19*2, rs4244285, c.681G > A; CYP2C19*3, rs4986893, c.636G > A; and CYP2C19*17, rs12248560, c.806C > T). SAST system offers a novel method for clinical single-base mutation detection and is expected to find broad applications in early cancer diagnosis and precision medicine.

title: Advantages, considerations and challenges in using Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy to monitor tissue integrity and cell differentiation in Microphysiological Systems.
authors: Steger-Polt MH, Thomas YRJ, Pham P, Mailley P
abstract: Over the past few decades, the scientific community has become increasingly aware of the limitations of extrapolating animal models to humans. Consequently, microphysiological systems (MPS), such as spheroids, organoids, and organ-on-chip (OOC) technologies, have been suggested as pertinent alternatives. By combining cell biology, microfluidics, tissue engineering and materials science, these technologies reconstruct the 3D properties of biological cells and tissues in-vitro to provide physiological relevant models for drug screening, disease modelling and personalized medicine. However, transitioning MPS into straightforward tools for clinical investigations requires integrating sensors for non-invasive, continuous, and live monitoring. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) addresses this by taking advantage of the electrical properties of biological tissues that provide biophysical information associated with tissue integrity, cell viability and differentiation. This review addresses EIS in the context of MPS from a biological, an electrochemical, and an electrical point of view, with a fundamental emphasis on the selection of electrode materials and the complex electrode-electrolyte interface. We provide an in-depth evaluation of how electrode material properties impact the sensitivity of the interrogation system and discuss technical approaches to tackle these challenges. Furthermore, we challenge the incoherent use of the generic term "TEER" within the community, prompting us to introduce the distinct notions of TEERsqrw, TEERsine, and TEEReqm to better account for the nature of the measurements and enable refined data analysis and comparability. By bridging these perspectives, this review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of current systems and to serve as a strategic guide for future experimental designs.

title: Hormone-sparing non-surgical male contraception in dogs and cats: Current strategies and the emerging role of FSH receptor-targeted antibody fragments.
authors: Navanukraw P, Kunkitti P, Chatdarong K
abstract: Surgical reproductive control remains the most widely used method for reproductive control in dogs and cats, but it requires anesthesia, trained personnel, surgical facilities, and post-operative care, which may limit its application in large-scale free-roaming animal populations. In males, orchidectomy also eliminates Leydig cell testosterone production, removes negative feedback on the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, and may contribute to persistent elevation of luteinizing hormone. These endocrine changes have increased interest in hormone-sparing contraceptive strategies that suppress fertility without fully reproducing the hormonal consequences of castration. This review summarizes current non-surgical male contraceptive approaches in dogs and cats, including GnRH agonists, progestogens, androgens, systemic chemical contraceptive agents, intratesticular and intraepididymal chemical contraceptive agents, therapeutic ultrasonography, gene-editing strategies, and immunological approaches. Many existing methods suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, damage testicular tissue, require repeated administration, or have inconsistent effects on testosterone preservation. In contrast, follicle-stimulating hormone receptor (FSHr)-targeted antibody fragments offer a more selective approach by targeting Sertoli cell support of spermatogenesis while avoiding direct interference with LH-mediated Leydig cell testosterone production. Recent studies in dogs and cats have demonstrated species-specific anti-FSHr antibody fragments that suppress Sertoli cell functional markers in vitro, while in vivo evidence from long-tailed macaques suggests that anti-FSHr scFv can impair sperm output and semen quality without significantly altering serum testosterone concentrations. Although further in vivo studies are required in dogs and cats, anti-FSHr antibody fragments represent a promising emerging direction for hormone-sparing male contraception in companion animals.

title: Understanding genetic determinants of bacterial adaptation to plant niches: Toward more robust bioinoculant design.
authors: Villa-Rodríguez E, Ferguson S, Stougaard J, Radutoiu S
abstract: Plant-associated bacteria offer a sustainable alternative to chemical inputs in agriculture, yet the field performance of microbial inoculants remains inconsistent. A central but frequently overlooked cause is that bioprospecting pipelines still select strains on the basis of plant-growth-promoting activities, while the bacterial genetic traits that determine whether a strain can reach, colonise and persist in a given root compartment are rarely assessed. Previous reviews have largely catalogued growth-promoting functions or described root microbiome assembly from the plant's perspective, here we take the bacterium's. We trace the journey of a bacterium from bulk soil to its final niche and, at each stage, identify the genes and pathways (genetic determinants) that encode key bacterial traits involved, such as chemotaxis and motility, nutrient acquisition and metabolic independence, competitive and defensive arsenals, attachment and biofilm formation, evasion of plant immunity, and endophytic entry and persistence. Throughout, we use evidence from comparative genomics and metagenomics, (meta)transcriptomics, targeted mutagenesis and genome-wide screens such as Tn-seq, obtained in systems ranging from binary interactions to synthetic communities and natural soils. For each stage we examine the current state of knowledge, identify critical gaps, and propose avenues to deepen our mechanistic understanding of the bacterial traits involved in plant colonisation. We argue that this mechanistic understanding is the missing foundation for developing inoculants with more consistent and robust performance across diverse agroecosystems.

title: From passive fillers to active implants: A 3D-printed trilayer piezoelectric scaffold recapitulating native bone hierarchy.
authors: Shan Y, Li S, Wang Y, Lei Y, Wang G, Zhou Q, Lu Y, Wu Y
abstract: Critical-sized alveolar bone defects affect over 10 million patients annually, yet current synthetic bone substitutes act as passive osteoconductive fillers with unpredictable outcomes. Native bone, by contrast, achieves robust regeneration through a trilayered hierarchy of cancellous, cortical, and metabolically active periosteal tissues, with intrinsic piezoelectricity converting mechanical loading into endogenous electrical cues. While piezoelectric biomaterials have emerged as promising active implants, existing homogeneous scaffolds fail to recapitulate native bone's structural complexity and electromechanical coupling; to date, no work has combined this trilayer architecture with piezoelectric functionality in a single construct. Here we report a trilayer bioinspired piezoelectric scaffold fabricated via a two-step conformal 3D printing strategy, composed of a strontium-doped β-tricalcium phosphate (Sr-β-TCP) triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) cancellous layer, a dense cortical layer, and a barium titanate/silk fibroin (BTO/SF) piezoelectric periosteal layer. Under non-invasive low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) stimulation, the scaffold generates bioelectrical signals that support robust osteogenic activity and pro-angiogenic potential in vitro. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that these electrical cues are associated with intracellular calcium influx and upregulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) and Wnt/β-catenin pathways, consistent with enhanced osteogenic differentiation. In a critical-sized bone defect model, the trilayer scaffold with LIPUS achieves substantially superior bone regeneration relative to controls. This work pioneers the integration of native bone hierarchy with piezoelectric functionality into a single active construct, shifting bone tissue engineering from passive filling to bioelectric-guided repair. Coupling structural biomimicry with electroactive stimulation, this strategy holds potential for future bone regenerative applications, including alveolar bone reconstruction.

title: Micellar LYTAC-engineered bionic coatings abrogate RANK-dependent osteocatabolism and boost fibrillogenesis-mimetic mineral accretion for empowering osteoporotic osseointegration.
authors: Zhao Y, Zhou J, He Y, Ren Y, Zhang J, Chen M, Luo Z, Gong Z
abstract: Patients with osteoporosis are highly susceptible to fractures that often require implant fixation and stabilization. However, excessive osteoclast activity under osteoporotic conditions accelerates bone resorption at the bone-implant interface, severely compromising implant osseointegration. RANKL-RANK axis is a central regulator of osteoclast function and emerges as a promising target for osteoporosis treatment, yet current therapeutic options primarily rely on reversible ligand neutralization and can be followed by rebound bone loss after treatment discontinuation. Here, we developed a biomimetic titanium implant coating incorporating RANK-targeted micellar lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) to enhance osseointegration under osteoporotic conditions. Collagen-like peptides (CLPs) were conjugated to bispecific aptamers targeting RANK and the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor (CI-M6PR) through acid-responsive linkers. The resulting conjugates self-assembled into supramolecular LYTACs (CLP-Apt) and were integrated onto hydroxyapatite-modified titanium surfaces. Hydroxyapatite facilitated mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) recruitment, whereas acidic microenvironmental cues triggered CLP-Apt release. Simultaneous engagement of RANK and CI-M6PR on osteoclasts directed RANK toward lysosomal degradation, thereby suppressing osteoclast-mediated bone resorption while promoting MSC osteogenic differentiation and type H vessel formation. Following lysosomal processing, the released CLPs assembled extracellularly into bone matrix-mimetic fibers that chelated Ca2+ and accelerated new bone formation through a fibrillogenesis-mimetic process. By directly degrading RANK while promoting vascularized bone regeneration, this coating provides a localized strategy to overcome osteoclast-driven implant failure and achieve rapid, robust osseointegration under osteoporotic conditions.

title: Pretransplant immune dysregulation and survival after HSCT in pediatric inborn errors of immunity.
authors: Soffia A, Borzutzky A, Sotomayor C
abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative for many inborn errors of immunity (IEIs), but the prognostic role of pretransplant immune dysregulation in pediatric patients remains unclear. We retrospectively studied 29 pediatric patients with genetically confirmed IEI undergoing HSCT between 2021 and 2025. Immune dysregulation was quantified using IDDA v2.1; HCT-CI and PARI were also calculated. 2-year overall survival (OS) was 79%, and event-free survival was 59%. Higher IDDA v2.1 scores were associated with inferior OS in univariate analysis (HR: 2.23 per five-point increase, P = 0.043) and remained associated in an exploratory multivariable model (HR: 2.76, P = 0.041). Harrell's C-statistic for OS was 0.722 for IDDA v2.1, 0.661 for HCT-CI, and 0.772 for PARI. Exploratory quadrant analyses suggested that IDDA v2.1 provides complementary information, identifying patients classified as lower risk by comorbidity indices who nonetheless had adverse outcomes. These findings support IDDA v2.1 as an adjunct pretransplant risk stratification tool in pediatric IEI.

title: Reproductive biology and conservation breeding of viverrids in Thailand.
authors: Thongphakdee A, Sangsuri R, Punyatong R, Nakas T, Vechmanus T, Siriaroonrat B, Kamolnorranath S, Susereedumrong J
abstract: In Thailand, nine viverrid species, including the small Indian civet (Viverricula indica), have traditionally been valued for musk used in traditional medicine. Despite their cultural and economic importance, information on their reproductive biology and captive breeding has remained limited. In 2008, Her Majesty Queen Sirikit the Queen Mother initiated a royal conservation project focused on viverrid research and propagation. The program aimed to: (1) establish conservation breeding protocols for small Indian civets, (2) characterize estrous cycles and reproductive hormone profiles, and (3) evaluate male reproductive anatomy and semen characteristics in five viverrid species: small Indian civets, large Indian civets (Viverra zibetha), large-spotted civets (Viverra megaspila), common palm civets (Paradoxurus hermaphroditus), and masked palm civet (Paguma larvata). Results demonstrated that small Indian civets breed throughout the year, with a gestation period of 64-69 days. The breeding program successfully produced 59 kittens, with litter sizes ranging from 1 to 4 offspring. Fecal hormone analyses from nine females monitored over 12 months revealed a polyestrous reproductive pattern, with peak reproductive activity occurring from February to July. The mean estrous cycle length was 18.6 ± 4.2 days. Male reproductive morphology and semen characteristics varied among species, and copulatory plugs were identified in both small Indian civets and large Indian civets during semen collection. The project also extended practical husbandry and breeding knowledge to local farmers through community-based knowledge transfer initiatives. Overall, this study provides novel insights into viverrid reproductive biology and conservation breeding, supporting sustainable population management and reducing pressure from wild capture and hunting.

title: Temporal dynamics of systemic immune cell networks in C57BL/6 mice with collagen-induced arthritis.
authors: Liu L, Hu Y, Liu H, Jin P, Yang S, Zhang H, Wan X
abstract: Collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) model in C57BL/6 (H-2b background) mice provides a valuable model for studying the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). However, the immune mechanism underlying this model remains unclear. This study aims to comprehensively understand the dynamic multi-dimensional characteristics of CIA, especially the temporal changes in immune cell subsets, providing a basis for future research on immune-targeted therapy for RA. The CIA course was divided into onset, peak, and chronic stages based on arthritis scores. Joint pathology was assessed by histology; immune cell subsets in the spleen and lymph nodes were profiled by flow cytometry; and serum cytokines were measured by ELISA. The results revealed distinct stage-specific immune alterations during CIA progression. M1 polarization occurred at the onset stage. DCs were markedly activated at the peak stage, accompanied by elevated frequencies of Th1, Th17, and Tfh cells, while the Breg cell proportions declined. Moreover, DC activation and abundant Th1 and Tfh cells persisted into the chronic stage. Neutrophils remained elevated throughout disease progression to sustain inflammatory responses. Furthermore, upregulated TNF-α and decreased TGF-β1 represented the core cytokine alterations driving CIA pathogenesis. Collectively, this study provided in-depth insights into dynamic immune shifts during CIA progression and offered valuable clues for developing novel RA immunotherapies.

title: Programmable histone acetylation enables reversible regulation of cellulase production in Myceliophthora thermophila.
authors: Li Y, Zhao X, Yang X, Wang J, Liu D, Yu Q, Liu Q, Tian C
abstract: Myceliophthora thermophila is a thermophilic filamentous fungus with great potential for biomass biorefining and industrial protein production. However, the locus-specific epigenetic regulation of the cellulolytic network in this fungus remains poorly understood. Here, we established a CRISPR/dCas9-p300 system that recruits the p300 histone acetyltransferase to target loci and targeted the promoters of the key cellulolytic regulators clr-1, clr-2, and xyr-1. Targeted recruitment of dCas9-p300 increased the transcription of these regulators by up to 5.2-fold and promoter-associated histone acetylation by approximately 2- to 3-fold. Simultaneous targeting of all three regulators resulted in greater increases than single-locus targeting, with extracellular protein production and CMCase activity increasing by up to 5.5- and 3.7-fold, respectively. The dependence of these effects on guide RNA-directed targeting and p300 catalytic activity was confirmed using no-guide controls and the p300 inhibitor A-485. A catalytically inactive p300 mutant targeting clr-2 failed to enhance clr-2 transcription, extracellular protein production, or CMCase activity. We further developed an inducible dCas9-p300 system to examine the persistence and reversibility of the activated state. Following inducer withdrawal, the high cellulase-production phenotype was maintained during the initial propagation but gradually declined over successive passages and was restored upon re-induction. These results demonstrate that targeted histone acetylation can coordinately activate an endogenous cellulolytic regulatory network and establish a reversible high-production state without altering the DNA sequences of the target loci. This work provides a chromatin-based strategy for reversible regulation of endogenous gene networks and protein production in filamentous fungi.

title: Zygote origin shapes sensitivity to electrical voltage field and editing susceptibility after CRISPR/Cas9-RNP electroporation in bovine embryos.
authors: Rahimi M, Miskel D, Schreiber M, Habermann H, Haake L, Brenig B, Besenfelder U, Havlicek V
abstract: Despite major progress in generation of edited embryos and offspring via CRISPR/Cas9-RNP electroporation, editing outcomes remain highly variable. This variability may be due to intrinsic differences between in vivo-derived (IVV) and in vitro-derived (IVT) zygotes, which may play a more decisive role than previously anticipated. Therefore, this study aimed to determine how zygote origin shapes the sensitivity to electrical voltage field and editing susceptibility after CRISPR/Cas9-RNP electroporation in the bovine model. The present study systematically compared subsequent developmental competence and editing events in IVV- and IVT-derived bovine zygotes across defined electroporation voltages and pulse durations. Notably, CRISPR/Cas9-RNP electroporation of IVV-derived bovine zygotes of comparable age and collected by tubal embryo flushing (10-18 h post ovulation, hpo) resulted in markedly lower survival rates at 25 and 30 V compared to 20 V. In contrast, higher (p < 0.05) editing frequencies were observed at 25 V and 30 V. Clear differences, however, were observed between the two zygote groups. Following CRISPR/Cas9 RNP electroporation, IVV-derived zygotes yielded a higher proportion of unedited blastocysts (p < 0.05), absence of full edited embryos, a significantly increased frequency of monoallelic edits and reduced rates of mosaicism compared to IVT-derived zygotes. Collectively, the results of the present study clearly underscore a significant lower editing efficiency to pulse sensitivity ratio in IVV-derived zygotes compared to their IVT counterparts. To our knowledge, this is the first study to use bovine IVV-derived zygotes for genome editing using RNP-electroporation to elucidate how zygote origin shapes sensitivity to electrical voltage field and editing efficiency.

title: Aptamer-functionalized EGCG nanocarrier for neutrophil-targeted AKBA delivery promotes anxiety-related fracture healing.
authors: Ouyang L, Zhang Y, Liao J, Zhang Z, He X, Lin Z, Tao R, Xie X
abstract: Anxiety is clinically associated with impaired fracture healing, but the underlying immunological mechanism remains unclear, and no targeted therapy is available. In a mouse model of chronic restraint stress (CRS)-induced anxiety with femoral fracture, we observed expansion of TGFβ1+CCR5+ double-positive neutrophils in the bone marrow. These neutrophils inhibited osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) via TGFβ1 secretion, while BMSC-derived CCL5 reciprocally promoted neutrophil activation, forming a detrimental feedback that disrupted fracture repair. Mechanistically, CRS activated the NF-κB-CCR5 axis to upregulate CCR5 and sustain this neutrophil subset. We found that acetyl-11-keto-β-boswellic acid (AKBA) directly bound YAP1, relieved YAP1-mediated suppression of ubiquitin-specific peptidase 31 (USP31), and consequently inhibited NF-κB phosphorylation and CCR5 expression, reducing the pathogenic neutrophil population and restoring BMSCs' osteogenic function. In order to overcome the problems of poor solubility, low bioavailability and tissue non-selectivity of AKBA, we developed a NIMP-R14 aptamer-modified epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG)-coated nanocarrier (AKBA@E-N), which can achieve enhanced uptake and local retention of neutrophils in the acidic microenvironment of the fracture site. In vivo, AKBA@E-N significantly accelerated fracture healing compared with free AKBA. This study reveals a neutrophil-mediated mechanism linking stress to impaired bone repair and provides a targeted nanotherapeutic strategy.

title: Inhibition of WNT signaling sensitizes CRC cells to anti-tumor effects of retinoids: basis for new drug combinations in oncology.
authors: Hunsu VO, Facey COB, Opdenaker LM, Boman BM
abstract: Our Goal is to sensitize human colorectal cancer (CRC) to the differentiation-inducing effects of retinoic acid (RA) agents by suppressing WNT signaling. Previously, we reported that the WNT and RA pathways are functionally linked, and in CRC, APC mutation generates a WNT:RA imbalance leading to incomplete differentiation and stem cell (SC) overpopulation. Hypothesis: Therapeutically inhibiting WNT signaling enhances the ability of retinoid agents to induce growth suppression and differentiation. We tested drug combinations of: (1) anti-WNT agents (Sulindac & Piroxicam) that produce anti-tumor activity in humans and animals harboring germline APC mutations, with (2) RA agents (All-trans-RA, 9-cis RA) and RA metabolism blocking agent (CYP26A1 inhibitors Liarozole and Talarozole), which inhibit proliferation and induce differentiation of CRC cell lines. Results: The combined effect of anti-WNT agents and RA drugs shows additive or synergistic responses in CRC cell lines compared to single agents. Drug combinations decrease the proportion of aldehyde dehydrogenase-positive SCs and increase neuroendocrine cell differentiation in CRC cells that show a synergistic response to treatment. NanoString profiling shows that therapeutically decreasing WNT signaling in CRC cells significantly changes the effect of RA signaling on gene expression. Treating human CRC organoid cultures and PDX mouse models with WNT:RA-based drug combinations led to greater anti-tumor activity as compared to individual agents. Conclusion: Inhibiting WNT signaling effectively sensitizes CRC cells to the anti-tumor effects of retinoids. These findings have important clinical significance for designing new drug combinations against CRC.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Feasibility and potential benefits of daily online adaptive radiotherapy for head and neck cancer without margin reduction using an RTT-only workflow.
authors: Lindegaard AM, Håkansson K, Appelt A, Bernsdorf M, Gothelf AB, Jensen TRB, Mohammad A, Kristensen CA
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Online adaptive radiotherapy (oART) may improve head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, where anatomical changes during radiotherapy (RT) are common. However, oART is resource-intensive and clinical data are limited. We conducted a prospective feasibility trial implementating an RT technologist (RTT)-led workflow to evaluate dosimetric outcomes, workflow strategies, and intrafractional motion in daily oART. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Ten patients receiving curatively intended oART (33-34 fractions) using standard PTV margins were included (NCT: 07506902). For each fraction, a scheduled plan (original plan recalculated on daily anatomy) and an adapted plan (reoptimized to daily anatomy) were generated, and the preferred plan was delivered. Target coverage (PTV1 V95%), mean dose (Dmean) and maximum dose (Dmax) to selected organs at risk (OAR), treatment time, and baseline target volume were extracted for all fractions. The effect of oART (scheduled- versus delivered plan) was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Intrafractional motion was assessed weekly. RESULTS: A total of 322 adaptive session were completed. The median treatment time was 29.9 min. The adapted plan was selected in 78% of fractions. oART improved target coverage in 76% of fractions. Dmean decreased for the oral cavity (-2.4 Gy, p < 0.001) but increased for the middle PCM (2.5 Gy, p < 0.001). Dmax increased for the brainstem (2.9 Gy, p < 0.001) and spinal cord (2.2 Gy, p < 0.001). Intrafractional motion was within PTV margins, with few patient-specific exceedances. CONCLUSION: Daily oART for HNC is feasible with improvements in target coverage but modest and inconsistent OAR sparing.

title: Neuroanatomical subtypes of bulimia nervosa show divergent gray matter patterns and distinct clinical profiles.
authors: Wu M, Peng S, Chen Y, Guo L, He Q, Wang Y, Wang Q, Chen J
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bulimia nervosa (BN) is a clinically heterogeneous eating disorder. Variability in clinical presentation and treatment response suggests differences in underlying neurobiology. Neuroimaging studies have reported inconsistent findings of widespread brain structural alterations in BN, which may reflect unrecognized neuroanatomical subtypes. Identifying such subtypes could inform targeted treatment approaches. METHODS: 81 treatment-naïve female Han Chinese patients with BN and 72 healthy controls from a single center underwent T1-weighted MRI. Computational Anatomy Toolbox 12 was used to quantify regional gray matter volumes (GMVs). The heterogeneity through discriminative analysis (HYDRA) algorithm was applied to identify neuroanatomical subtypes. Neuroanatomical characteristics of the subtypes were compared, and clinical characteristics were compared in 55 patients with available clinical assessments. RESULTS: Two distinct BN subtypes with divergent GMV aberrations and clinical characteristics were identified. Subtype 1 exhibited widespread GMV reductions mainly involving the cerebellum, prefrontal, temporal, parietal, and occipital cortices, insula, and limbic regions. It was characterized by higher depressive symptoms, younger age, and lower estimated total intracranial volume (eTIV), with eTIV negatively correlated with eating disorder psychopathology, particularly weight and shape concerns. Subtype 2 showed relatively preserved GMV, with alterations restricted to the right cerebellum. In this subtype, emotion dysregulation showed a subtype-specific association with eating disorder psychopathology. CONCLUSION: Two neuroanatomical subtypes of BN are characterized by distinct structural patterns and clinical profiles. Subtype 2 patients may benefit from emotion regulation-focused interventions, while those with Subtype 1 may benefit from more comprehensive treatment. These implications remain hypothetical and require validation in longitudinal interventional studies.

title: Clinical, Cytological, and Virological Factors Associated with Histological Severity and Recurrence in Vaginal Intraepithelial Neoplasia: A Retrospective Observational Study.
authors: Della Corte L, Palumbo M, Foreste V, Boccia D, Bifulco G, Lavitola G
journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VAIN) is a rare HPV-related condition with heterogeneous behavior and a relevant recurrence risk. Factors associated with severity and recurrence remain incompletely defined. OBJECTIVE: To explore clinical, cytological, virological, and colposcopic features associated with high-grade VAIN and recurrence. METHODS: This retrospective study included 42 women with histologically confirmed VAIN at a tertiary center between January 2020 and January 2026. All underwent vaginal cytology, high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotyping, colposcopy, and biopsy. Histology was classified as VAIN1 or VAIN2-3. Recurrence was defined as a histologically confirmed lesion after treatment and documented disease-free assessment. Associations were assessed using bivariate and exact analyses. RESULTS: VAIN2-3 was diagnosed in 31 women (73.8%). Among HR-HPV-positive women, HPV16-related infection was more frequent in VAIN2-3 than VAIN1 (65.4% vs 18.2%; OR 8.50, 95% CI 1.27-91.56; p = 0.013). Cytology was associated with histological grade (p = 0.024); all women with HSIL/ASC-H had VAIN2-3, although sensitivity was limited. Over a median follow-up of 24 months, eight women (19.0%) recurred after a median of 11.5 months. HPV16-related infection was more frequent with recurrence (75.0% vs 38.2%; OR 4.85, 95% CI 0.70-54.01; p = 0.112), but the evidence was not definitive. HPV16-only infection showed borderline evidence of association (p = 0.050), while no clear outcome pattern emerged for multiple-genotype infection. No other significant associations with recurrence were observed. CONCLUSION: HPV16-related infection was associated with high-grade histology among HR-HPV-positive women, while its prognostic relevance for recurrence remains uncertain. The limited sensitivity of cytology underscores the value of multimodal assessment. These exploratory signals warrant prospective validation.

title: Trait-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze-like response resistance.
authors: Kučera J, Makarová M, Vít M, Novák J, Zlámal F, Ráčková L, Fialová Kučerová J, Grulichová M
abstract: The freeze-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals (n = 20) with experienced police rapid response personnel (n = 20). Freeze-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze-like responses. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre- to post-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze-resistance may be associated with stable, trait-like signatures rather than acute stress-responsive processes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze-resistance (r = 0.75, p = 4 × 10-9) and training status (r = 0.71, p = 6 × 10-8), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass (r = 0.57, p = 8 × 10-5). This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms.

title: Self-assembled ruthenium(II) nanostructures disrupt electron transport and energy metabolism in MRSA via bacterial interfacial interactions.
authors: Tang Z, Liu D, Zhang W, Chen Y, Tang J, Luo Z, Li L, Chen L
journal: Journal of colloid and interface science
abstract: The emergence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) has substantially compromised the effectiveness of conventional antibiotic therapies, highlighting the need for alternative antibacterial strategies. Herein, we designed an amphiphilic ruthenium(II) complex(Ru1) that spontaneously self-assembles into highly cationic nanostructures in aqueous media. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that hydrophobic interactions among long alkyl chains and van der Waals interactions contribute significantly to the self-assembly process. The resulting cationic nanostructures preferentially interact with LTA-rich MRSA cell-envelope interfaces through electrostatic interactions, leading to membrane potential disruption, electron transport chain dysfunction, NAD+/NADH imbalance, and reduced ATP production, ultimately causing bacterial energy metabolic dysfunction. Ru1 exhibited potent antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against MRSA. Furthermore, Ru1 effectively reduced bacterial burden in murine wound and systemic infection models while maintaining favorable biocompatibility. This study provides insights into the role of amphiphilic molecular design and self-assembled interfaces in regulating bacterial interactions and antibacterial activity of Ru(II)-based nanostructures.

title: Association Between Serum Amylin, Irisin, and Sirtuin 1 in Male Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Diabetic Nephropathy.
authors: Sabih Wajdi S, Mohyadini M, Abdlwhab HM, E Jassim W, Bathaie SZ
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) is a progressive disease worldwide that leads to various complications. Given the roles of the hormones amylin and irisin and the enzyme sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) in metabolism and oxidative stress, we focused on these parameters in the serum of patients. OBJECTIVES: We investigated the associations between serum amylin, irisin, and SIRT1 levels and diabetic nephropathy (DN), an important complication of DM. METHODS: Patients with DM (n = 50) and DN (n = 50) were included in this single-center cross-sectional study. Various parameters were measured from fasting blood and urine samples. Serum amylin, irisin, and SIRT1 levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kits. In addition to demographic characteristics, fasting blood sugar, glycated hemoglobin, serum insulin, urine creatinine, and estimated glomerular filtration rate were used to classify participants. RESULTS: After adjustment for age, diabetes duration, body mass index, fasting blood sugar, glycated hemoglobin, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, amylin levels were significantly lower, whereas irisin and SIRT1 levels were significantly higher, in the DN group than in the DM group. Multivariable logistic regression showed that higher amylin levels were associated with lower odds of DN, whereas higher irisin and SIRT1 levels were associated with higher odds of DN. Receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate the ability of these biomarkers to discriminate between the DM and DN groups. In addition, mediation analysis showed associations among irisin, SIRT1, and DN. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that irisin and SIRT1 are associated with DN status in patients with diabetes and may provide insights into metabolic complications. However, longitudinal studies are needed to establish causality.

title: Nutrient availability and sodium pyruvate regulate the resuscitation of viable but nonculturable Staphylococcus aureus.
authors: Yu H, Ge R, Du J, Hua Y, Zhao F
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) can enter a viable but nonculturable (VBNC) state when induced by citric acid at 4 °C, posing hidden risks to food safety upon resuscitation. However, the effects of nutritional conditions and sodium pyruvate (SP) on this process remain unclear. This study demonstrates that 0.5 × TSB, TSB, 2 × TSB, and SP resuscitate VBNC cells following sigmoidal kinetics, with an efficacy ranking of SP > 2 × TSB > TSB > 0.5 × TSB. SP significantly accelerated resuscitation through enhanced early enzymatic activity, a transient increase in intracellular ROS levels, and rapid ATP accumulation, accompanied by dynamic nucleic acid fluctuations peaking at 10-12 h. Furthermore, proteomic profiling and targeted inhibition analyses revealed that DNA repair and cell wall biosynthesis are critically involved in initiating resuscitation, whereas signal transduction and respiratory metabolism primarily govern post-resuscitation growth. Practically, a 5-h or 10-h pre-resuscitation in 2 × TSB successfully detected VBNC S. aureus in high pressure processing-treated apple juice during 4 °C storage, which was undetectable via direct enumeration. These findings offer mechanistic insights into pathogen resuscitation and provide practical strategies for food safety risk assessment and detection.

title: Integrated metabolite, volatile, and genome annotation profiling reveals distinct functional phenotypes in cocoa-derived yeasts.
authors: Ganiyu KO, Zhao J
abstract: Cocoa fermentation shapes the precursor chemistry underlying chocolate flavour, but the isolate-level contributions of cocoa-associated yeasts remain incompletely resolved. This study compared six cocoa-derived yeasts with a reference Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain by profiling sugar utilisation, organic-acid turnover, volatile formation, and targeted genome annotation under controlled cocoa-relevant conditions. In cocoa pulp extract-based medium, Kluyveromyces marxianus Y1A, Meyerozyma guilliermondii Y1, and Ogataea polymorpha Y3A showed the strongest sugar depletion and organic-acid transformation, whereas the Kwoniella isolates Y4 and Y6B retained larger residual sugar pools and Lodderomyces orthopsilosis Y5 showed an intermediate phenotype. In synthetic cocoa pulp-simulating medium, volatile profiles further separated isolates across medium-chain fatty acids, alcohols, esters, and carbonyls. Y3A showed sustained fatty acid ethyl ester-associated output, Y1A displayed an acetate-ester-biased profile, and Y4 showed strong ester-associated output despite weaker primary carbon-use performance. Targeted genome annotation showed broadly conserved support for central metabolic functions, with clearer differences in sucrose- and ester-associated features. Targeted homology searches clarified key genome-phenotype gaps by revealing candidate sucrose-utilisation homologues in Y1A and candidate ester-associated homologues in Y3A and Y4 that were not fully resolved by the automated annotation panel. Overall, the integrated dataset showed clear isolate-associated differences in carbon processing, organic-acid turnover, and volatile-associated metabolism. Y1A and Y3A showed the strongest overall profiles under the conditions tested, supporting further evaluation in mixed-culture and pilot-scale cocoa fermentation studies. The genome-based taxonomic assignments, safety status, technological robustness, and regulatory suitability should be further confirmed before any starter-culture application.

title: Changes in Hormone Cycles and Exercise Capacity During Testosterone Therapy in a Transmasculine Triathlete: A Case Study.
authors: St Pierre SR, Johnson SC, Muccini J, Bourne B, Laniakea BH, Delp SL, Hicks JL
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The impact of testosterone therapy on the hormone cycles, exercise capacity, and physiology of transmasculine individuals is not well understood. Existing studies report limited metrics at large time intervals between data collection points. METHODS: High-resolution temporal data were collected from a single amateur trans male triathlete over 13 months-including one baseline month and 12 months on testosterone therapy-to characterize hormone, strength, body composition, aerobic, and training load profiles. RESULTS: Daily urine hormone monitoring revealed that progesterone and luteinizing hormone are the clearest metrics associated with cessation of menses. After 1 yr, the participant increased lean body mass by 12%, average hand grip strength by 16%, jump height by 16%, and average knee isometric strength by 18%, but did not lose fat mass or show changes in isokinetic knee strength. Fluctuations in running fitness and maximum oxygen consumption (     V ˙    O  2 m a x       ) were associated with both training and testosterone levels, with future work needed to untangle their relative contributions. CONCLUSION: This study provides the most comprehensive characterization of the impacts of testosterone therapy on hormone cycles, exercise capacity, and physiological changes in a single person to date, as well as observations to help inform the design of larger cohort studies.

title: DNA-decorated phase-shift microdroplets enable programmable coalescence and gene transfection.
authors: Perilli G, Ditri A, Vitaliti A, Toumia Y, Porchetta A, Paradossi G, Domenici F
journal: Journal of colloid and interface science
abstract: HYPOTHESIS: Phase-shift perfluorocarbon microdroplets (MDs) are a promising and flexible method for challenging applications in colloid science, such as customizing chemical reactions or enhancing tumor gene delivery efficiency. To achieve these goals, we focused on stable MDs made of a decafluoropentane (DFP) core and a dimethyldioctadecylammonium bromide (DDAB) lipid shell that binds DNA through electrostatic interactions to create DNA-MDs assemblies. EXPERIMENTAL: The MDs were obtained via ultrasound homogenization and decorated with complementary DNAs. Fluorescence, confocal microscopy, and dynamic light scattering methodologies were combined to measure the binding features driving DNA-MDs formation and their coalescing interactions. The effect of the DNA-MDs at the cell interface was evaluated by MTT viability assay and DNA transfection in tumor melanoma cells. FINDINGS: We defined the colloidal formulation of DNA-MDs, functional for both chemical and biomedical relevant applications. First, we identified the conditions that enable DNA-MDs to rapidly and selectively coalesce via oligonucleotide hybridization at the MDs interface. Then, we used DNA-MDs to efficiently enter nucleic acids into human melanoma cells, even within a two-step transfection protocol to promote intracellular DNA strand displacement. Our results could shed new light on conducting controlled reactions in small volumes, realizing microreactors, as well as designing consensus gene transfection strategies.

title: Reprogramming NOX4-associated ferro-aging with an iron-chelating senescent-cell-targeted therapy for intervertebral disc degeneration.
authors: Wang J, Chen Q, Xing J, Sun Y, Yan C, Zhao B, Han L, Sun J
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) has been a major contributor to chronic low back pain, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Here, we identified a NOX4-associated ferro-aging program linking iron overload, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and cellular senescence in degenerative NPCs. Clinical imaging, transcriptomic analyses, human disc specimens, iron-overloaded NPCs, and naturally aged rats consistently revealed ferro-aging-associated changes during IVDD. Mechanistically, gain- and loss-of-function, genetic rescue, and temporal analyses positioned NOX4 as an upstream oxidative regulator of ROS-dependent ACSL4 activation, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and NPC senescence. Natural-product screening identified amentoflavone (Amen) as a candidate NOX4-interacting compound that suppresses membrane-associated NADPH oxidase activity in a NOX4-dependent manner. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses showed that ferro-aging NPCs exhibited increased NKG2D ligand-related stress signals, reduced endocytic activity, and enhanced membrane-fusion features. Guided by these characteristics, we engineered SenoFAN, an Amen-loaded, iron-chelating phenolic nanozyme coated with NKG2D-engineered NPC membranes. SenoFAN integrates iron sequestration, nanozyme-mediated redox remodeling, Amen-mediated NOX4-dependent suppression of NADPH oxidase activity, and ferro-aging-cell-adapted delivery through NKG2D-ligand recognition and membrane fusion. In vitro, SenoFAN reduced labile iron and oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial and lipid homeostasis, and suppressed lipid peroxidation and senescence. In a rat puncture-induced IVDD model, SenoFAN showed preferential association with ferro-aging-associated NPCs, prolonged intradiscal retention, reduced iron deposition and senescence, preserved disc structure, and showed favorable biosafety. Collectively, our findings identify NOX4-associated ferro-aging as a therapeutically actionable pathological program in IVDD, while establishing an upstream regulatory role for NOX4 in the FAC-induced ferro-aging model.

title: Discovery and characterization of potent and efficacious small-molecule parathyroid hormone Receptor-1 (PTH1R) antagonists for the treatment of hypercalcemia.
authors: Pontillo J, Wang S, Zhu Y, Rico-Bautista E, Shintaku J, Urgaonkar S, Antwan A, Betz SF
abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is caused by the enlargement and overactivation of one or more of the parathyroid glands, via parathyroid adenomas or hyperplasia. This results in over-secretion of PTH hormone, which results in agonism of PTH1R and subsequent hypercalcemia. Blocking PTH action via an oral, small-molecule PTH1R antagonist may provide a convenient and improved therapy for PHPT. Herein, we report the discovery, optimization and characterization of a highly potent, bioavailable and efficacious series represented by 9c (hPTH1R IC50 = 5.2 nM), which based on pharmacokinetics and biological activity, represents a significant preclinical advancement in the development of small-molecule PTH antagonists.

title: Integrated SEM, TEM and CLSM workflow for tegumental analysis of adult Schistosoma mansoni.
authors: de Carvalho Augusto R, João RCF, Barbosa HS, Mello-Silva CC, Santos CP
abstract: The tegument of Schistosoma mansoni is a key host-parasite interface and a major target for drug and vaccine development. Although ultrastructural studies of the tegument date back decades, methodological inconsistencies often complicate comparisons across studies. Here, we present a standardized, easy-to-use framework for investigating tegumental architecture using three complementary techniques: scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). We provide step-by-step protocols, highlight strengths and limitations of each method, and illustrate their outputs using adult male worms. We also outline a scheme for unbiased quantitative analysis of the resulting images and indicate how the protocols can be adapted to female worms, to other developmental stages and schistosome species, and to immunolocalization at the ultrastructural level. This integrative pipeline enables reproducible morphological characterization and facilitates downstream applications in pharmacology, immunology, and parasite biology.

title: Targeting tumor-selective membrane-associated PCNA enables selective antibody-drug conjugate therapy.
authors: Abu Ahmad M, Ungar-Malma NM, Naumchik A, Machluf-Katz N, Radinsky O, Adi Eisdorfer S, Gara A, Istoyler Y
abstract: Membrane-associated proliferating cell nuclear antigen (mPCNA) is an attractive tumor-selective antigen for antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) development. We generated a chimeric IgG1 ADC, RC14-MMAE, to exploit three key properties of mPCNA that support its use as an efficient delivery platform. First, flow-cytometric and imaging analyses show abundant mPCNA surface expression on multiple tumor cell lines and in JIMT1 xenografts, providing accessible epitopes for binding. Second, comparative profiling against non-malignant counterparts and normal mouse tissues reveals minimal or undetectable mPCNA at the plasma membrane of healthy cells, indicating a sharp tumor-normal differential expected to limit off-tumor targeting and improve the therapeutic window. Third, live-cell internalization assays demonstrate that RC14 rapidly accumulates in LAMP1-positive lysosomes after engaging mPCNA, confirming efficient trafficking along the endolysosomal pathway required for protease-mediated cleavage of the valine-citrulline linker and release of monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). Consistent with this target profile, RC14-MMAE exhibits potent antigen-dependent cytotoxicity in mPCNA-positive tumor models in NSG mice, favorable pharmacokinetics, sustained payload retention in serum, robust in vivo antitumor activity with limited overt toxicity, and a significantly increased fraction of F4/80⁺ tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells within dissociated tumors. These findings establish mPCNA as a functionally validated, tumor-selective internalizing target and support RC14-MMAE as a first-in-class mPCNA-directed ADC with broad translational potential.
